summary: Four items worked, all four re-verified against the current tree before touching code; two live defects FIXED, one established as LATENT-ONLY and partially closed with its residue written into the file, one pair of narrowings landed (one in a file I own, one referred). Plus an end-to-end read of src/tok/api.py as a unit, which found three more things and refuted none of the confirmer's. ITEM 1 REPRODUCED AND FIXED: the re-segmentation no-op cache served a stale `labels` vector -- at the shipped TOK_DROPOUT=0.0, three calls on the same bytes object with labels None / [0]*n / [7]*n all returned THE SAME OBJECT with .labels None, under tok.retok_noop 2. Fixed by keying the entry on `labels` by identity (a 7-field tuple); the neighbour -- same labels object twice -- still takes the skip, and the composition root's exact call shape is byte-identical before and after (tok.retok_noop 2, bytes_per_token 2.741857394 both). EVERY arm that reads the cache is now enumerated in Vocabulary.__init__, input by input, so a fourth reader does not have to find the next one. ITEM 2 REPRODUCED AND FIXED at the configuration tok/levers.py has on record: TOK_MAX_BYTES=6 with TOK_SEED_VOCAB=2000 printed tok.build_converged=1 -- 'the corpus ran out of pairs' -- on a build that stalled at 464/2000 with NINE pairs still at or above min_pair, the top of them b' quebec ' at 162 and eight bytes long, refused for LENGTH alone. Fixed by counting refusals apart (tok.build_refused) and gating the converged row on refused == 0; at the shipped TOK_MAX_BYTES=16 the row still reads 1 with zero pairs remaining, and at TOK_MIN_PAIR=100000 the true convergence still reads 1. No behaviour removed: the break is unchanged, vocabulary sizes and mint counts identical on every arm, and the RNG stream does not move (identical draw counts and identical next draw before/after). ITEM 3 IS LATENT ONLY AND I SAY SO PLAINLY: it cannot produce a wrong reading today. ITEM 4: the ckpt cost-(2) paragraph -- every measurement in it false against the current spine/units.py -- is rewritten; the eval/api.py half is REFERRED with an exact find/replace and the referral written into ckpt/api.py rather than left in an audit file. Suite green, 23 couplings / 19 wires of 25 / 4 intra-package UNCHANGED -- no edge spent. Two files edited, both mine. No commit, no push, nothing under tests/** or runs/** touched, every scratch script outside the repository.

findings.symbol: src/tok/api.py::tokenize (ITEM 1 -- the no-op cache served a stale `labels` in a second arm)
findings.detail: REPRODUCED FIRST, ON THE COMMITTED TREE, BEFORE ANY EDIT. The cache entry was (data, start, len(data), stamp, Segmentation, drawn_with_dropout) and `labels` -- an ARGUMENT of tokenize -- was in none of the six fields, while the cached Segmentation carries `labels=out_labels` computed from the labels of the call that BUILT it. So a later call on the same bytes object with a different `labels` argument, the None -> not-None direction included, was handed the earlier call's label vector and counted as tok.retok_noop, a row whose whole meaning is 'the rebuild would have been byte-identical'. It IS identical in `ids` and `byte_pos` and is NOT in `labels`. tokenize's own docstring makes that channel load-bearing ('it takes the label of its FIRST byte ... so a per-area score and a byte offset always agree') and the one live call site, src/spine/compose.py:2008 `tok_api.tokenize(tok, sysm.vocab, sysm.stream.bytes, sysm.stream.labels, regularize=True, seed=int(run.seed))`, does pass them. FIXED THE SAME WAY THE DROPOUT ARM WAS: the entry stays a valid STAMP (still written unconditionally) and becomes an invalid ANSWER for a call that asked for different labels -- the guard gains `and cache[6] is labels` and the tuple gains a seventh field. Identity rather than equality is deliberate and matches `cache[0] is data`: O(1), and the composition root hands the same list object back on a re-tokenization of its own stream. AND THE THING THE TASK ASKED FOR BEYOND THE FIX -- EVERY ARM THAT READS THIS CACHE IS NOW ENUMERATED IN Vocabulary.__init__, input by input against tokenize's signature (data -> cache[0]+cache[2]; start -> cache[1]; labels -> cache[6]; regularize -> cache[5] for the entry and `drop <= 0.0` for this call; tok -> only tok.dropout, through `drop`; seed -> NOT COVERED and does not need to be, the body never reads it; vocab -> cache[3], the stamp, over the two structures _segment consults). Two of the seven were found one at a time by two separate readers; the list exists so the next one is not.
findings.repro: BEFORE (committed tree, one process, TOK_MODE=online TOK_SEED_VOCAB=320 TOK_DROPOUT=0.0, one Vocabulary, three calls on the SAME bytes object): 's0.labels: None / s1 is s0: True | s1.labels: None / s2 is s0: True | s2.labels: None / counters {... tok.segment: 1, tok.byte_fallback: 1839, tok.retok_noop: 2}'. AFTER (same script, same seed): 's1 is s0: False | s1.labels: [0,0,0,0,0] / s2 is s0: False | s2.labels: [7,7,7,7,7] / counters {... tok.segment: 3, tok.retok: 2}'. NEIGHBOUR A (same data, SAME labels object, twice): 'same object? True | labels[:3] [3,3,3]', counters {tok.segment: 1, tok.retok_noop: 1} -- the skip still fires. NEIGHBOUR A2 (labels=None twice): 'same object? True | labels None'. NEIGHBOUR B, the dropout arm the previous round fixed, still right in both directions at TOK_DROPOUT=0.3: 'det IS reg: False | lens reg/det/truth 8112 7118 7118 | det==truth: True', 'det,det same object? True' (the no-op is still REACHABLE at dropout>0), 'reg,reg same object? False lens 8140 8128 identical ids? False' (BPE-dropout is not frozen). NEIGHBOUR C, the composition root's exact call shape at the shipped default repeated three times: identical before and after -- 'all same object? True True | labels ok: [0,0,0]', tok.retok_noop 2, bytes_per_token 2.741857394 -- so the path measured at 2.189 b/B and 68 points of word quality is untouched. NO RNG SHIFT: before/after on the same script give identical regularized lengths [8112, 8140, 8128, 8143], identical tok.dropout_skip 7379, and an identical next stream draw 0.125087374517.

findings.symbol: src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary (ITEM 2 -- tok.build_converged printed the false equation its own comment exists to prevent)
findings.detail: REPRODUCED AT THE CONFIGURATION tok/levers.py HAS ON RECORD. The row r3 added hangs on `if minted == 0:` and asserts a CAUSE -- its comment reads 'CONVERGED MEANS THE CORPUS RAN OUT OF PAIRS'. I established by reading the loop that `minted == 0` has exactly TWO reachable causes, not three: the inner `vocab.size() >= target` break CANNOT produce it (size moves only when `_add` succeeds, and the outer loop already tested size >= target before entering), so it means either (a) the first candidate fell below min_pair -- the convergence the row claims -- or (b) every candidate at or above min_pair was REFUSED by `_add`, for len(seq) > max_bytes, for already existing, or at the cap. On (b) the tally is still full and the corpus is not exhausted. FIXED WITHOUT REMOVING ANYTHING: refusals are now counted (`refused`), written to a new declared counter tok.build_refused seeded to 0 beside the other three on the arm that runs the loop, and the converged row is written only when refused == 0. The BREAK is unchanged on both arms and that is not a narrowing -- nothing minted means the next pass re-segments identically, tallies identically, and refuses or falls short identically. The DID IT FIRE line and Vocabulary.__init__'s counters paragraph both name the fourth row, so it is declared where it is written. THE CITATION WAS OPENED AND CONFIRMED, not copied: src/tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.max_bytes (line 358) does contain, verbatim, 'measured "max_tok=6 vmax=4000 -> stalled at 658/4000 with 1866 pairs still above min_pair (83.5% dead)" (tokenizer.py:318-324)'. NO CHECK IN THE SUITE FAILS EITHER WAY AND I DO NOT CLAIM ONE DOES: K4 is about levers and nothing reads counters. The check that catches this is the tree's DID IT FIRE rule, enforced by reading.
findings.repro: Fresh process per configuration via lever._reopen_assembly() + rng.reset_issued(); 6000 random words from a 20-word list, one area, TOK_BUILD_BYTES=200000 TOK_SEED_VOCAB=2000 TOK_BUILD_PASSES=6, TOK_MIN_PAIR at its default 50; after each build the build sample is re-tallied against the finished vocabulary. BEFORE, TOK_MAX_BYTES=6: '{tok.build_pass: 4, tok.build_mint: 208, tok.build_converged: 1} size=464/2000; pairs still >= min_pair(50): 9  top=(b\' quebec \', 162)' -- eight bytes, refused for length alone, while the counter says the corpus was exhausted. BEFORE, TOK_MAX_BYTES=2: '{build_pass: 2, build_mint: 94, build_converged: 1} size=350/2000; pairs still >= min_pair: 88  top=(b\'echo\', 174)'. BEFORE, TOK_MAX_BYTES=16 (SHIPPED DEFAULT): '{build_pass: 5, build_mint: 219, build_converged: 1} size=475/2000; pairs still >= min_pair: 0' -- the row is TRUE at the default, which is exactly why it went unnoticed. AFTER: max_bytes=6 -> '{build_pass: 4, build_mint: 208, build_converged: 0, build_refused: 19} size=464/2000'; max_bytes=2 -> '{build_pass: 2, build_mint: 94, build_converged: 0, build_refused: 88} size=350/2000' (88 refused against 88 pairs remaining -- the ledger is now checkable against the corpus); max_bytes=16 -> '{build_pass: 5, build_mint: 219, build_converged: 1, build_refused: 0}' UNCHANGED. Sizes and mint counts identical before and after on all three -- only the counters moved. NEIGHBOURS, one fresh process each: TOK_MIN_PAIR=100000 -> '{build_pass: 1, build_mint: 0, build_converged: 1, build_refused: 0}', the TRUE convergence still reported; mode=bytes -> '{tok.segment: 1, tok.byte_fallback: 12397}', all four build keys ABSENT; replay arm (hand-written parent dyntok.json, CKPT_RESUME set) -> '{tok.load_reconciled: 1, tok.load_reconciled_detail: (...)}' with no build key and the gate reading 'UNREACHABLE (None vs 8) -- resumed via d_vocab_read_path...'; mode=fixed -> gate 'FIRED (2 vs 8)'.

findings.symbol: src/tok/api.py::tokenize (ITEM 3 -- the stamp does not cover len(vocab.retired))
findings.detail: IT CAN ONLY PRODUCE A WRONG READING AFTER A STUB LANDS. IT CANNOT PRODUCE ONE TODAY, PLAINLY. Established by grep and by reading, not by assumption: `grep -rn '\.retired' src/ tests/ tools/` returns exactly three live sites in src/tok/api.py -- `self.retired = set()` in __init__, `len(self.retired)` in live_size, and `retired = vocab.retired` in _segment. NOTHING ANYWHERE WRITES TO IT. `Vocabulary` has no retire() method at all (its methods are size, live_size, at_cap, _cap, blen, decode, _add), and the body that the docstrings say would retire, tok/api.py::judge_probation, is `raise NotImplementedError` (as is mint_burst, which owns reinstatement). So len(vocab.retired) is 0 on every reachable configuration and the third term changes no value in this tree. FIXED ANYWAY, BECAUSE IT COSTS NOTHING AND _segment CONSULTS TWO STRUCTURES: `s2i.get(...)` and `if j is None or j in retired: continue`, so a stamp over seq2id alone was a stamp over PART of the match table. stamp is now (size, len(seq2id), len(retired)) and the docstring says so. AND HERE IS THE NARROWING I OWE, WHICH THE PROPOSED FIX DID NOT STATE: THE THIRD TERM DOES NOT CLOSE THE SECOND SHAPE ITS OWN JUSTIFICATION NAMES. Under the retirement this package describes -- pop from seq2id, add to retired -- a retire of one id paired with a REINSTATEMENT of a different retired id in the same flush moves len(seq2id) by -1 then +1 AND len(retired) by +1 then -1, BOTH to a net zero, while the match table has genuinely changed. No count of the two sets can see that; only a monotone revision number bumped by every match-table mutation can, and there is nothing to bump it in yet. That residue is now written into the file beside the fix rather than left for a fifth reader to file as a fresh defect against the same cache. It is also in unfinished.
findings.repro: grep: `grep -rn '\.retired' src/ tests/ tools/` -> src/tok/api.py:114 `self.retired = set()`, :173 `len(self.id2bytes) - len(self.retired)`, :610 `s2i, mlbf, retired = vocab.seq2id, vocab.mlbf, vocab.retired`; plus prose in spine/compose.py. `grep -n 'def retire' src/` -> no definition anywhere. `grep -n 'raise NotImplementedError' src/tok/api.py` -> seven stubs including judge_probation and mint_burst. Behaviourally: every arm run above prints len(retired)==0, so the stamp value is identical before and after the edit -- the compose-shaped neighbour returns bytes_per_token 2.741857394 and tok.retok_noop 2 on both trees.
